Prometheus Fire-bearer was the title of a satyr play of Aeschylus (fr. 187-199), which is called Prometheus Fire-burner by Pollux 9, 156, who had in mind Sophocles' play entitled Nauplius Fire-burner: on which I have spoken at fr. 187.

The interpreters took this as said for πόθεν πόθεν [whence, whence], a Doric form of the adverb, on which see Thes. vol. 6 p. 2293, but it is not likely that Aeschylus used it, who without doubt wrote πῶς πῶς [how, how], as corrected in the margin of Askew.

Joined with the negatives οὐ and μή it coalesces into one word οὔπω and μήπω, on which see in their proper place. With a word interposed.
